title: How many CME hours do physicians need in each state?
description: Physician CME hours, cycles and mandated topics in California, Texas, Florida, Pennsylvania, Illinois and New York, from board sources, as at November 2026.
shortAnswer: Physician continuing medical education (CME) in the United States is set by each state medical board, so hours, cycles and mandated topics differ. As at November 2026, California requires 50 hours every two years, Texas 48 hours every 24 months, Florida 40 hours per biennium, Pennsylvania 100 hours every two years and Illinois 150 hours every three years. New York sets topic mandates such as infection control, child abuse reporting and opioid prescriber education rather than an hours total.
keyTakeaways: Each state medical board sets its own CME hours, cycle and mandated topics; there is no national physician CME requirement, apart from the federal one-time DEA training for prescribers.

Opioid and controlled substance content is the most common mandate: Florida every biennium for DEA registrants, Pennsylvania every renewal for DEA registrants, Texas every 8 years, and New York every 3 years.
Texas has added mandates on human trafficking, nutrition and metabolic health, and forensic evidence collection for ER physicians, with new start dates in 2027.
Pennsylvania added a one-time 2 hour organ and tissue donation requirement effective May 1, 2026, and New York mandated reporters must complete an updated child abuse curriculum by November 17, 2026.
Record retention ranges from 2 years after renewal in Pennsylvania to 4 years in California and Florida.
jurisdiction: United States (state medical boards: California, Texas, Florida, Pennsylvania, Illinois and New York)
regulator: State medical boards, including the Medical Board of California, Texas Medical Board, Florida Board of Medicine, Pennsylvania State Board of Medicine, Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation and New York State Education Department
appliesTo: Physicians (MD) holding active licenses in the states covered; osteopathic boards may differ
Hospital medical staff offices, credentialing teams and physician groups tracking CME across states
CME providers designing courses that must satisfy state topic mandates

sections.heading: Who sets physician CME requirements in the US?

blocks.text: State medical boards set them, through statute and board rules, as a condition of renewing a physician's license or registration. The result is a patchwork: total hours, cycle length, the share that must be accredited Category 1 credit, and the list of mandated topics all vary. Physicians licensed in several states must meet each state's rules separately, although one course can often count in more than one state.

The only nationwide training duty is federal and narrow: the one-time 8 hours of substance use disorder training for practitioners registered with the Drug Enforcement Administration, covered in [the DEA MATE Act requirement](/regulations/dea-mate-act-training-requirement). This page compares six large states, each checked on the board's own site or the official code.

sections.heading: What does California require of physicians?

blocks.text: California requires at least 50 hours of approved CME during each biennial renewal cycle, certified under penalty of perjury at renewal. The [Medical Board of California CME page](https://www.mbc.ca.gov/Licensing/Physicians-and-Surgeons/Renew/Current-Status/Continuing-Medical-Education.aspx) states that the board conducts an annual audit and that 16 CCR 1338(e) requires physicians to retain records for at least four years.

Most physicians must complete a one-time CME course in pain management and the treatment of terminally ill and dying patients, including the risks of addiction with Schedule II drugs. Physicians can meet it with 12 hours by their second renewal, or with a one-time 12 hour course on treating opiate dependent patients that includes 8 hours on buprenorphine or similar treatment. Pathologists and radiologists are exempt, and the 12 hours count toward the 50. The board accepts AMA PRA Category 1 programs and AAFP prescribed credit, and grants 100 hours of credit for four consecutive years to physicians who pass a recognized specialty board certifying or recertifying examination.

sections.heading: What does Texas require of physicians?

blocks.text: Texas requires at least 48 credits every 24 months, at least half in formal Category 1 or 1A courses, under Board Rule 161.35. The [Texas Medical Board CME page](https://www.tmb.texas.gov/apply-renew/physician/continuing-education-requirements-for-physicians) states that mandatory CE tracking through CE Broker began for all licensees on September 1, 2026, and that newly licensed physicians are exempt at their first registration.

items: **Ethics:** at least 2 of the 24 formal hours in medical ethics or professional responsibility.

**Pain management and opioids:** under Occupations Code 156.055, 2 formal hours within one year of license issuance and again at the second renewal, then every 8 years (every 4 renewals) for physicians in direct patient care.

**Human trafficking:** under Occupations Code 156.060, 1 hour in the first renewal period and every third renewal period after that, using an HHSC approved course, which counts as ethics or professional responsibility.
**Nutrition and metabolic health:** under Occupations Code 156.061, at least 1 hour each biennial renewal for licenses expiring on or after May 30, 2027.

**Forensic evidence collection:** House Bill 47 (89th Legislature) requires 2 hours for physicians and physician assistants treating patients in an emergency room setting; because no approved courses were available, the board starts it for licenses expiring February 28, 2027.

blocks.text: Physicians who provide obstetric care must also complete a free one-time course on pregnancy related medical emergencies under Senate Bill 31, the Life of the Mother Act, before they can renew.

sections.heading: What does Florida require of physicians?

blocks.text: Florida requires 40 hours of board approved CME in the 24 months before each biennial renewal, under [Rule 64B8-13.005](https://www.flrules.org/gateway/ruleNo.asp?id=64B8-13.005). The mandated content sits inside the 40 hours: 2 hours on prevention of medical errors covering root cause analysis and the five most misdiagnosed conditions named by the board, 2 hours of domestic violence every third biennium, and 1 hour on HIV/AIDS including Florida law at the first renewal.

Physicians registered with the DEA must also complete a board approved 2 hour course on prescribing controlled substances at each biennial renewal under [section 456.0301, Florida Statutes](https://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&URL=0400-0499/0456/Sections/0456.0301.html), which requires coverage of opiate prescribing standards, nonpharmacological therapies, emergency opioid antagonists and sickle cell pain. The department may not renew a DEA registered prescriber who has not completed it. Florida physicians also completed a one-time 1 hour human trafficking course by January 1, 2021 under section 456.0341.

sections.heading: What does Pennsylvania require of physicians?

blocks.text: Pennsylvania requires 100 credit hours of CME in the preceding biennial period, including at least 2 hours of approved child abuse recognition and reporting training, under [49 Pa. Code 16.19](https://www.pacodeandbulletin.gov/Display/pacode?file=/secure/pacode/data/049/chapter16/s16.19.html). At least 20 hours must be AMA PRA Category 1, and at least 12 must be in patient safety and risk management.

A physician holding or using a DEA registration must complete at least 2 hours in pain management, identification of addiction, or the practices of prescribing or dispensing opioids. An amendment effective April 25, 2026 added a one-time 2 credit hour requirement in organ and tissue donation and recovery, effective May 1, 2026, to be completed within 5 years of licensure renewal for existing licensees. Physicians must keep documentation for 2 years after renewal for random audits.

sections.heading: What do Illinois and New York require of physicians?

blocks.text: Illinois requires 150 hours of CME per prerenewal period, defined as the 36 months preceding July 31 in the renewal year, under [68 Ill. Adm. Code 1285.110](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/illinois/Ill-Admin-Code-tit-68-SS-1285.110). At least 60 hours must be formal CME and up to 90 may be informal, first renewals are exempt, and the AMA Physician's Recognition Award certificate is accepted as proof. The department extended the 2026 physician renewal deadline to August 31, 2026.

New York's mandates are topic based. Physicians complete infection control and barrier precautions training at initial licensure and every four years under Public Health Law section 239, according to the [State Education Department](https://www.op.nysed.gov/professions/physicians/mandated-training-related-infection-control), and child abuse identification and reporting training under Education Law section 6507(3)(a). Prescribers with a DEA registration complete 3 hours in pain management, palliative care and addiction every three years and attest to the Department of Health.

blocks.title: New York deadline: November 17, 2026
blocks.text: The State Education Department states that Chapter 25 of the Laws of 2024 requires mandated reporters, including those already trained, to complete updated child abuse coursework on children with intellectual or developmental disabilities by November 17, 2026. Those trained between November 1, 2022 and August 31, 2025 can take a short addendum.

sections.heading: How should a multistate medical group evidence physician CME?

blocks.text: Track each mandate as a separate obligation with its own cycle and trigger, and attach certificates that name the topic, the accreditation and the hours. Triggers such as DEA registration, ER assignment or obstetric practice decide who owes what, so they belong in the physician's record alongside the license state. The steps in [how to map training to compliance obligations](/guides/how-to-map-training-to-compliance-obligations) apply directly, and [how to prepare training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit) covers the file itself.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry represents each state mandate as a node with its source, cycle and trigger, so one accredited opioid course can be shown to satisfy Florida, Pennsylvania and federal duties at once while remaining separately evidenced. When a board adds a topic, as Texas and Pennsylvania did in 2026, the change is made once and flows to every affected physician. See [healthcare and life sciences](/industries/healthcare-life-sciences).

faqs.q: Does board certification satisfy state CME requirements?
faqs.a: Sometimes, partly. Texas presumes compliance for physicians who become board certified or recertified in the preceding 36 months, or who are meeting maintenance of certification CME, but not for every mandated topic. California grants 100 hours of credit for four years after passing a recognized specialty board examination. Check each state's mandated topics separately.

faqs.q: Can one CME course count in more than one state?
faqs.a: Usually, if each board accepts the accreditation and the content meets each state's topic definition. AMA PRA Category 1 credit is widely accepted. Topic mandates with prescribed content, such as Florida's controlled substance course from listed providers or Texas's HHSC approved trafficking course, may not transfer.

faqs.q: Which states require implicit bias training for physicians?
faqs.a: This page does not list implicit bias mandates for physicians because they could not be confirmed on the board pages reviewed for these six states. New York's updated child abuse curriculum includes protocols to reduce implicit bias in decision making for mandated reporters. Check each board directly for current implicit bias rules.

faqs.q: Do physicians need to send CME certificates when renewing?
faqs.a: Generally no. California, Florida and Pennsylvania rely on attestation backed by random audits. Texas requires reporting through CE Broker as part of mandatory tracking from September 1, 2026.
